formulas.name: Double sided CI for population mean (t-distribution, algebraic derivation)
formulas.expression: X_bar ~ N(mu, sigma/sqrt(n)); (X_bar-mu)/(s/sqrt(n)) ~ t(n-1); P[t_0.025,n-1 <= (X_bar-mu)/(s/sqrt(n)) <= t_0.975,n-1] = 95% => P[X_bar - t_0.975,n-1 * s/sqrt(n) <= mu <= X_bar - t_0.025,n-1 * s/sqrt(n)] = 95% => P[X_bar - t_0.975,n-1 * s/sqrt(n) <= mu <= X_bar + t_0.97 ,n-1 * s/sqrt(n)] = 95% (t(n-1) is symmetric)

symbols.t_p,df: p-th quantile of Student t with df degrees of freedom

formulas.conditions: sample size n sufficiently large (Central Limit Theorem); course notes the t-distribution works for almost any distribution of X provided n not too small

formulas.name: Double sided approximate CI for population fraction defectives pi (normal approximation)
formulas.expression: P ~ N(pi, sqrt(pi(1-pi)/n)); (P-pi)/sqrt(pi(1-pi)/n) ~ Z; P[Z_0.025 <= (P-pi)/sqrt(pi(1-pi)/n) <= Z_0.975] = 95% => P[P - Z_0.975*sqrt(pi(1-pi)/n) <= pi <= P + Z_0.975*sqrt(pi(1-pi)/n)] = 95% => P[p - Z_0.975*sqrt(p(1-p)/n) <= pi <= p + Z_0.975*sqrt(p(1-p)/n)] ≅ 95% (approximately, pi replaced by sample p)
formulas.conditions: n sufficiently large; note text: at least 5 defectives need to turn up in the sample (e.g. defective fraction 1% needs n>=500)

formulas.name: One sided CI notation
formulas.expression: one-sided (1-alpha)x100%-CI ]pi_L, 1] (lower-bounded) or [0, pi_U[ (upper-bounded)
formulas.conditions: constructed by plotting only the (1-alpha)x100%-quantile of the sample distribution (one tail) instead of both tails

formulas.name: Rule of thumb: accuracy vs sample size (95% CI, worst case p=50%)
formulas.expression: doubling the accuracy (halving CI width) corresponds to quadrupling the sample size: n=100 -> width=20%; n=400 -> width=10%; n=1350 -> width=5%

symbols.width: width of the 95% confidence interval for a proportion at p=50%

formulas.conditions: worst case p=50% (largest CI width in absolute terms)

formulas.name: Betrouwbaarheidsinterval definitie (Z, sigma gekend)
formulas.expression: P[|x_bar - mu| <= 1.96*sigma/sqrt(n)] = 95% <=> P[x_bar - 1.96*sigma/sqrt(n) <= mu <= x_bar + 1.96*sigma/sqrt(n)] = 95%
formulas.conditions: sigma verondersteld gekend

formulas.name: t-statistiek en t-verdeling van Student (definitie)
formulas.expression: Z ~ N(0,1), X ~ chi²(n), Z en X onafhankelijk => t ≡ Z/sqrt(X/n) ~ t(n); t symmetrisch en klokvormig; E(t)=0; lim(n->oneindig) t(n) = Z
formulas.conditions: Z en X onafhankelijk

formulas.name: Link tussen t-statistiek (X_bar,s) en t-verdeling
formulas.expression: X normaal: X~N(mu,sigma) => (X_bar-mu)/(sigma/sqrt(n)) ~ Z en (n-1)s²/sigma² ~ chi²(n-1) => t=(X_bar-mu)/(s/sqrt(n)) ~ t(n-1). X niet normaal: X_bar nog steeds normaal (CLS) maar (n-1)s²/sigma² niet langer chi² verdeeld => t-statistiek niet exact t-verdeeld, voor praktijk toch meestal OK (robuustheid)
formulas.conditions: robuustheid geldt behalve bij combinatie van kleine steekproef en sterk niet-normale verdeling

formulas.name: Betrouwbaarheidsinterval voor mu (t-gebaseerd) vs Z-gebaseerd (sigma gekend)
formulas.expression: P[-t_0.025 <= (X_bar-mu)/(s/sqrt(n)) <= t_0.025] = 95% => x_bar - t_0.025*s/sqrt(n) <= mu <= x_bar + t_0.025*s/sqrt(n)  (95%-BI op basis van t); vergelijk met x_bar - Z_0.025*sigma/sqrt(n) <= mu <= x_bar + Z_0.025*sigma/sqrt(n)  (95%-BI op basis van Z, sigma gekend)
formulas.conditions: sigma -> s introduceert meer onzekerheid: groter BI voor zelfde betrouwbaarheid

formulas.name: BI voor mu1-mu2, niet-paarsgewijs, sigma gekend en gelijk
formulas.expression: X1_bar ~ N(mu1, sigma/sqrt(n1)), X2_bar ~ N(mu2, sigma/sqrt(n2)) => X1_bar - X2_bar ~ N(mu1-mu2, sqrt(2/n)*sigma) (n1=n2=n); BI95 = (x1_bar - x2_bar) ± Z_0.025*sqrt(2/n)*sigma
formulas.conditions: stel n1=n2=n en sigma1=sigma2=sigma gekend

formulas.name: BI voor mu1-mu2, paarsgewijs, sigma_V gekend
formulas.expression: V_bar = LD1_bar - LD2_bar; sigma²(LD1_bar - LD2_bar) = 2(sigma²-cov)/n => LD1_bar-LD2_bar ~ N(mu1-mu2, sqrt((2/n)(sigma²-cov))); BI95 = (x1_bar-x2_bar) ± Z_0.025*sqrt((2/n)(sigma²-cov))

symbols.cov: covariantie tussen LD1 en LD2 binnen een paar

formulas.conditions: stel sigma_V gekend; LD1 en LD2 positief gecorreleerde kenmerken (zelfde jongen)

formulas.name: Verhouding lengte BI paarsgewijs vs niet-paarsgewijs
formulas.expression: sqrt((2/n)(sigma²-cov)) / sqrt((2/n)*sigma²) = sqrt(1 - cov/sigma²) = sqrt(1-rho)

symbols.rho: correlatiecoefficient tussen LD1 en LD2 binnen paar

formulas.conditions: hoe groter rho, hoe kleiner de verhouding (nauwkeuriger paarsgewijze vergelijking)

formulas.name: BI voor mu1-mu2, niet-paarsgewijs, sigma ongekend maar gelijk (pooled t)
formulas.expression: X1_bar ~ N(mu1,sigma/sqrt(n1)), X2_bar ~ N(mu2,sigma/sqrt(n2)) onafh. => X1_bar-X2_bar ~ N(mu1-mu2, sigma*sqrt(1/n1+1/n2)); (n1-1)s1²/sigma² ~ chi²(n1-1), (n2-1)s2²/sigma² ~ chi²(n2-1) onafh. som => [(n1-1)s1²+(n2-1)s2²]/sigma² ~ chi²(n1+n2-2); => [(X1_bar-X2_bar)-(mu1-mu2)] / [s_p*sqrt(1/n1+1/n2)] ~ t(n1+n2-2), waarbij s_p² = [(n1-1)s1²+(n2-1)s2²] / (n1+n2-1) [zo afgedrukt op de slide]; 95%-BI: mu1-mu2 = (X1_bar-X2_bar) ± t_0.025,n1+n2-2 * s_p*sqrt(1/n1+1/n2)
formulas.conditions: enkel geldig als sigma1=sigma2; normaliteit van X1,X2 enkel echt nodig als n1 of n2 klein is

formulas.name: BI voor mu1-mu2, paarsgewijs, sigma_V ongekend
formulas.expression: V_bar ~ N(mu1-mu2, sigma_V/sqrt(n)); (n-1)s_V²/sigma_V² ~ chi²(n-1) => [V_bar-(mu1-mu2)]/(s_V/sqrt(n)) ~ t(n-1); 95%-BI: mu1-mu2 = v_bar ± t_0.025,n-1 * s_V/sqrt(n)

symbols.v_bar: gemiddelde van de verschillen v_i = x1_i - x2_i

formulas.conditions: spreidingen van LD1 en LD2 hoeven niet gelijk te zijn bij paarsgewijze vergelijking

formulas.name: Betrouwbaarheidsinterval voor pi
formulas.expression: P ~ N(pi, sqrt(pi(1-pi)/n)) => P[pi - Z_0.025*sqrt(pi(1-pi)/n) <= P <= pi + Z_0.025*sqrt(pi(1-pi)/n)] = 95% => benaderd 95%-BI obv P: p - Z_0.025*sqrt(p(1-p)/n) <= pi <= p + Z_0.025*sqrt(p(1-p)/n). Verschil van twee proporties (grote steekproeven): (pi1-pi2) = (p1-p2) ± Z_0.025*sqrt(p1(1-p1)/n1 + p2(1-p2)/n2)
formulas.conditions: n voldoende groot voor normale benadering; exacte methode op basis van binomiaalverdeling ook vermeld (grafische methode / nomogram)

formulas.name: Betrouwbaarheidsinterval voor sigma²
formulas.expression: (n-1)s²/sigma² ~ chi²(n-1) => P[chi²_0.975,n-1 <= (n-1)s²/sigma² <= chi²_0.025,n-1] = 95% => 95%-BI: (n-1)s²/chi²_0.025,n-1 <= sigma² <= (n-1)s²/chi²_0.975,n-1
formulas.conditions: niet symmetrisch interval; X normaal verdeeld

formulas.name: Tolerantie-interval voor normale verdeling (spreiding gekend)
formulas.expression: LTL = Y_bar - k*sigma; UTL = Y_bar + k*sigma; k = Z_(1-alpha)/sqrt(n) + Z_(1-beta) (enkelzijdig); dubbelzijdig: [Y_bar - k*sigma, Y_bar + k*sigma] = [Y_bar - (Z_(1-alpha/2)/sqrt(n) + Z_(1-beta/2))*sigma, Y_bar + (Z_(1-alpha/2)/sqrt(n) + Z_(1-beta/2))*sigma]
formulas.conditions: X (of Y=lnX) normaal verdeeld met gekende spreiding sigma

formulas.name: Tolerantie-interval voor normale verdeling (spreiding ongekend, k' benadering)
formulas.expression: [Y_bar - k'*s, Y_bar + k'*s] waarbij k' ≈ t(alpha/2,beta/2,n); enkelzijdig: [Y_bar - k*s, +infinity[ resp. ]-infinity, Y_bar + k*s] met k ≈ t(alpha,beta,n); t(alpha,beta,n) = Z_(1-beta)/(1-Z_(1-alpha)²/2n) + Z_(1-alpha)*(1+Z_beta²/2 - Z_(1-alpha)²/2n)^0.5 / (sqrt(n)*(1-Z_(1-alpha)²/2n))
formulas.conditions: spreiding sigma ongekend, geschat door s

formulas.name: Distributie-vrij tolerantie-interval
formulas.expression: [x_(1), x_(n)] is een (1-alpha,1-beta) tolerantie-interval wanneer n voldoende groot is om te voldoen aan (1-beta/2)^n - (1/2)(1-beta)^n <= alpha/2
formulas.conditions: distributie van X ongeacht de vorm, moet wel continu zijn

formulas.name: Test statistic - example t-test for the mean (case: manufacturing process)
formulas.expression: test statistic = (X_bar - 10) / (s/sqrt(n))
formulas.conditions: reference distribution = t(19)

formulas.name: Test statistic - example chi²-test for the standard deviation
formulas.expression: test statistic = (n-1)*s²/sigma²
formulas.conditions: reference distribution = chi²(19); classical quantity for testing the variance of a distribution

formulas.name: Power / OC-curve relation
formulas.expression: psi(lambda) = 1 - OC(lambda)

symbols.OC(lambda): Operating Characteristic - probability of accepting H0 (type-II risk) as a function of lambda
symbols.lambda: (mu-mu0)/sigma, gestandaardiseerde afstand tussen werkelijkheid en H0

formulas.conditions: kracht = kans op terecht verwerpen van H0; relatieve efficiëntie van test T1 t.o.v. T2 = n/m waarbij m de steekproeflengte is waarvoor T1 dezelfde kracht heeft als T2 op steekproeflengte n

formulas.name: Recept eenzijdige test - kritische waarde (voorbeeld beeldbuizen)
formulas.expression: kritische waarde in rechter staart = mu0 + Z_(1-alpha)*sigma/sqrt(n); cijfervoorbeeld: 1200 + 2.3*30 = 1270
formulas.conditions: H0: mu=mu0=1200; HA: mu>1200; alpha=1%

formulas.name: Recept dubbelzijdige test - kritische waarden (voorbeeld beeldbuizen)
formulas.expression: linkse kritische waarde = mu0 - Z_(1-alpha/2)*sigma/sqrt(n); rechtse kritische waarde = mu0 + Z_(1-alpha/2)*sigma/sqrt(n); cijfervoorbeeld: links 1200 - 2.6*30 = 1123; rechts 1200 + 2.6*30 = 1277

formulas.name: De link naar betrouwbaarheidsintervallen (algemene definitie)
formulas.expression: L_alpha(T) = inf{theta : T <= K_bar_alpha(theta)}; U_alpha(T) = sup{theta : T >= K_alpha(theta)}; dan is [L_alpha(T), U_alpha(T)] een (1-alpha)x100% BI voor theta

symbols.K_bar_alpha(theta), K_alpha(theta): boven- en ondergrens van het aanvaardingsgebied [K_alpha(theta0), K_bar_alpha(theta0)] voor H0: theta=theta0

formulas.conditions: K_bar_alpha(theta) en K_alpha(theta) zijn stijgende functies van theta

formulas.name: Exacte BI voor pi op basis van de binomiaalverdeling (grafische methode)
formulas.expression: K_alpha(pi) = (1/n) * B^-1(alpha/2; n; pi); K_bar_alpha(pi) = (1/n) * B^-1(1-alpha/2; n; pi); voorbeeld: p=0.6, n=200 => BI = [0.53, 0.67]

symbols.B^-1(q;n;pi): inverse van de binomiale cumulatieve verdeling (kwantiel)

formulas.conditions: in R: binom.test(120,200) levert BI = [0.53, 0.67]

formulas.name: t-test voor mu (testrecept)
formulas.expression: H0: mu = mu0 vs. (DZ) HA: mu != mu0 of (EZ) HA: mu > (<) mu0; statistiek t = (x_bar - mu0) / (s/sqrt(n)); onder H0 (X normaal): t ~ t(n-1)
formulas.conditions: parametrische test: X normaal verdeeld; robuustheid: algemeen toepasbaar behalve kleine RS + sterk niet-normale verdeling

formulas.name: Niet-paarsgewijze t-test voor mu1-mu2 (testrecept)
formulas.expression: H0: mu1=mu2 vs. (DZ) HA: mu1 != mu2 of (EZ) HA: mu1 > (<) mu2; t = (x1_bar - x2_bar) / (s_p*sqrt(1/n1+1/n2)) waarbij s_p² = [(n1-1)s1² + (n2-1)s2²] / (n1+n2-2); uitbreiding H0: mu1-mu2=d => t = (x1_bar-x2_bar-d) / (s_p*sqrt(1/n1+1/n2))
formulas.conditions: parametrische test: X1,X2 normaal verdeeld; bijkomende voorwaarde sigma1=sigma2; dan t ~ t(n1+n2-2); indien sigma1 != sigma2 manifest, aanpassen test

formulas.name: Paarsgewijze t-test voor mu1-mu2 (testrecept)
formulas.expression: H0: mu1=mu2 vs. (DZ) HA: mu1 != mu2 of (EZ) HA: mu1 > (<) mu2; verschillen v_i = x1_i - x2_i; t = v_bar / (s_v/sqrt(n)); uitbreiding H0: mu1-mu2=d => t = (v_bar - d)/(s_v/sqrt(n))
formulas.conditions: parametrische test: X1,X2 normaal verdeeld; dan t ~ t(n-1); hier geen voorwaarde sigma1=sigma2

formulas.name: Z-test voor pi (testrecept)
formulas.expression: H0: pi = pi0 vs. (DZ) HA: pi != pi0 of (EZ) HA: pi > (<) pi0; z = (p - pi0) / sqrt(pi0(1-pi0)/n); met continuïteitscorrectie: z = (p ± 1/(2n) - pi0) / sqrt(pi0(1-pi0)/n)  (+ links, - rechts staart; let op bij DZ)
formulas.conditions: Z ~ N(0,1) slechts benaderd geldig, voorwaarde n*pi0 > 5; indien n*pi0 < 5, werk met exacte distributie van P onder H0 (bij DZ via BI)

formulas.name: chi²-test voor sigma (testrecept)
formulas.expression: H0: sigma = sigma0 vs. (DZ) HA: sigma != sigma0 of (EZ) HA: sigma > (<) sigma0; statistiek = (n-1)*s²/sigma0²
formulas.conditions: parametrische test: X normaal verdeeld; dan statistiek ~ chi²(n-1); test is niet robuust (sterk gevoelig aan niet-normaliteit van X)

formulas.name: F-distributie (definitie en kritische waarden)
formulas.expression: X ~ chi²(n), Y ~ chi²(m), X en Y onafhankelijk => (X/n)/(Y/m) ~ F(n,m); stelling: RS1 -> n1,s1²; RS2 -> n2,s2² onafhankelijk => (s1²/sigma1²)/(s2²/sigma2²) ~ F(n1-1,n2-1); kritische waarden: F_alpha(n,m) = 1/F_(1-alpha)(m,n); E(F(n,m)) = m/(m-2) (m>2); mode(F(n,m)) = (n-2)m/(n(m+2)) (n>2)
formulas.conditions: n.v.t.

formulas.name: F-test voor sigma1/sigma2 (testrecept)
formulas.expression: H0: sigma1=sigma2 vs. (DZ) HA: sigma1 != sigma2 of (EZ) HA: sigma1 > (<) sigma2; F = s1²/s2² of F = s2²/s1²

symbols.s1,s2: steekproefspreidingen van RS1 (n1) en RS2 (n2), beide onafhankelijk

formulas.conditions: parametrische test: X1,X2 normaal verdeeld; dan F ~ F(n1-1,n2-1) of F(n2-1,n1-1) (keuze van F wordt gemaakt rekening houdend met beschikbare kritische waarden in de tabellen, enkel voor probabiliteiten < 0.5); test is niet robuust

formulas.name: chi²-test 'goodness of fit' (testrecept)
formulas.expression: H0: distributie van X heeft vooropgestelde gedaante; statistiek = som_k=1^r (e_k - n_k)² / e_k, waarbij e_k = n*pi_k, pi_k = P[X in klasse k]

symbols.n_k: waargenomen absolute frequentie in klasse k
symbols.e_k: verwachte absolute frequentie in klasse k onder H0

formulas.conditions: niet parametrisch: statistiek ~ chi²(r-g-1), slechts benaderd, voorwaarde e_k > 5; test is eenzijdig (EZ)

formulas.name: chi²-test 'contingency tables' (testrecept)
formulas.expression: H0: X en Y zijn onafhankelijk; statistiek = som_k=1^r som_l=1^s (n_kl - e_kl)² / e_kl, waarbij e_kl = n*pi_kl (onder H0: e_kl = n*pi_k.*pi_.l), geschat via pi_k. ≅ n_k./n en pi_.l ≅ n_.l/n zodat e_kl = n_k.*n_.l/n

symbols.r,s: aantal klassen voor X resp. Y

formulas.conditions: niet parametrisch: statistiek ~ chi²(rs-g-1), g=(r-1)(s-1)... vrijheidsgraden = (r-1)(s-1) [zoals afgedrukt: 'g = aantal te schatten parameters => aantal vrijheidsgraden = (r-1)(s-1)']; benaderd, voorwaarde e_kl > 5; bij 2x2-tabel: continuïteitscorrectie van Yates: n_ij < e_ij => n_ij + 1/2; n_ij > e_ij => n_ij - 1/2; test is EZ

formulas.name: Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney-test
formulas.expression: H0: nu1=nu2 vs. (DZ) HA: nu1 != nu2 of (EZ) HA: nu1 > (<) nu2; statistiek W_X1 = som van rangen geassocieerd aan X1-waarden (alle N=n1+n2 waarden samen gerangschikt); W_X1 discreet en symmetrisch; E(W_X1) = n1(N+1)/2; sigma²(W_X1) = n1*n2*(N+1)/12
formulas.conditions: niet parametrische test: vorm van X1,X2 niet vooropgesteld, wel: vorm van X1 en X2 gelijk; voor n1,n2<=10 tabel met kritische waarden; voor grotere n1,n2 benaderd normaal (Z-test, +continuïteitscorrectie); ties: gemiddelde rang toekennen

formulas.name: Wilcoxon signed ranks-test
formulas.expression: H0: nu1=nu2 vs. (DZ) HA: nu1 != nu2 of (EZ) HA: nu1 > (<) nu2; verschillen v_i = x1_i - x2_i, rangschikken in absolute waarde; statistiek T+ = som van rangen geassocieerd aan positieve verschillen; T+ discreet en symmetrisch; E(T+) = n(n+1)/4; sigma²(T+) = n(n+1)(2n+1)/24
formulas.conditions: niet parametrisch: vorm X1,X2 niet vooropgesteld, wel gelijke vorm; voor n<=15 tabel met kritische waarden (notatie n=N); voor n>15 T+ benaderd normaal (Z-test +continuïteitscorrectie); twee soorten ties: v_i=0 elimineren en n aanpassen; opeenvolgende gelijke abs. waarden: gemiddelde rang

formulas.name: Runs-test (Wald-Wolfowitz-test)

formulas.name: Excel: simulated CI for the mean (formulas used in demonstration workbook)
formulas.expression: sample value = _xlfn.NORM.INV(RAND(), mean, stddev); Xbar = AVERAGE(range); s = _xlfn.STDEV.S(range); Lower = Xbar - _xlfn.T.INV((1+confidence)/2, n-1) * s/SQRT(n); Upper-lower (width) = 2 * _xlfn.T.INV((1+confidence)/2, n-1) * s/SQRT(n); coverage indicator = IF(AND(Lower<=true_mean, true_mean<=Lower+width),1,0); achieved confidence = SUM(indicators)/number_of_samples
formulas.conditions: values are re-randomized on every recalculation (F9); cached values captured at extraction time gave an achieved confidence of 0.93 over 100 simulated samples (will differ on recalculation)

formulas.name: Excel: OC-curve for (n,c) acceptance sampling plan
formulas.expression: P[d<=c] = _xlfn.BINOM.DIST(c, n, pi, TRUE)
formulas.conditions: reproduces the 3 confirmation points of the (100,4) OC-curve: pi=1.30% -> 99%, pi=2.45% -> 90%, pi=7.85% -> 10% (matches CI PDF p14)

formulas.name: Excel: nomogram CI for fraction defectives - exact binomial
formulas.expression: lower quantile = _xlfn.BINOM.INV(n, pi, (1-confidence)/2) / n; upper quantile = _xlfn.BINOM.INV(n, pi, confidence+(1-confidence)/2) / n
formulas.conditions: large generated table (1121 rows), not transcribed - see topic entry

formulas.name: Excel: nomogram CI for fraction defectives - normal approximation
formulas.expression: lower bound = MAX(pi + _xlfn.NORM.INV((1-confidence)/2, 0, 1) * SQRT(pi*(1-pi)/n), 0)
formulas.conditions: clipped at 0 via MAX()

conventions.as_stated: No single default is stated; the course presents both a one-sided ('eenzijdige') and a two-sided ('dubbelzijdige') recipe as parallel, equally valid procedures, chosen according to the hypothesis: 'eenzijdige test geschikt om verschil in één richting te ontdekken; verschillen in beide richtingen ontdekken: dubbelzijdige test' and 'een eenzijdige test presteert wel beter in de gekozen richting: groter onderscheidingsvermogen of kracht' (Testing of Hypotheses - Further Reading (Dutch), p12/p14). Test recipes document formulates every specific test with both a (DZ) two-sided and (EZ) one-sided HA option.

No universal fixed default alpha is stated. alpha is described as a design parameter that 'moet a priori bepaald worden' and on which involved parties should agree up-front ('Involved parties should agree on the risks of the procedure up-front', Testing of Hypotheses.pdf p4). Worked examples in the course use different values of alpha depending on context: 5% (acceptance-sampling case example, CI PDF p3-4 and p13; OC-curve examples TH PDF p6-9), 1% (beeldbuizen example, TH Dutch FR p10/p13), 2% (t-test/chi²-test examples, TH PDF p12-13 and matching xlsx sheets), 98% confidence (=1-2% alpha, CI PDF p15-16).

conventions.topic: n vs n-1 in standard deviation
conventions.as_stated: Sample standard deviation/variance is consistently computed with the n-1 (Bessel-corrected) divisor, denoted s (or s²), e.g. '(n-1)s²/sigma² ~ chi²(n-1)' (CI Dutch FR p21; TR Dutch p11). In both xlsx workbooks the Excel functions used are _xlfn.STDEV.S and _xlfn.VAR.S (n-1 divisor), never STDEV.P/VAR.P.

'gebruik Z = (X_bar-mu)/(sigma/sqrt(n)) voor BI mu onrealistisch: sigma ??; praktijk: gebruik zg. t-statistiek' (CI Dutch FR p5). The course states the Z-test for mu is 'niet courant voor mu, komt wel te pas in andere situaties' (i.e. Z is mainly a teaching/illustrative device or used when sigma is genuinely known, e.g. tolerance intervals with known sigma, or the proportion pi tests where the reference distribution is naturally normal/binomial) - t is used whenever sigma must be estimated from the sample.

NORM.INV(RAND(),mean,sd) for simulating normal samples; T.INV((1+confidence)/2,df) for a two-sided critical t-value; T.INV(1-significance,df) for a one-sided critical t-value; T.DIST(x,df,cumulative) for density/p-value; T.TEST(array1,array2,tails,type) used as an independent cross-check of the p-value; CHISQ.INV(probability,df) is used directly with 'probability'=confidence (e.g. CHISQ.INV(0.98,19)) or with probability=1-significance (equivalent when confidence=1-alpha) to obtain the upper one-sided critical chi² value - CHISQ.INV.RT is never used in this course's workbooks; CHISQ.DIST(x,df,cumulative) with 1-CHISQ.DIST(...) used for a right-tail p-value; BINOM.DIST(x,n,p,cumulative) for OC-curves and lot acceptance probability; BINOM.INV(trials,prob,alpha) for the exact binomial CI nomogram; HYPGEOM.DIST(sample_s,number_sample,population_s,number_pop,cumulative) for the finite-population OC-curve; F.DIST(x,df1,df2,cumulative) used only to draw F density curves (no worked F-test example provided in the spreadsheets).

Both approaches are presented as fully equivalent: 'Consequently, a decision can be made by directly comparing the p-value with the significance alpha, no need for a determining the critical value anymore' (Testing of Hypotheses.pdf p10); 'beter: rechtstreekse vergelijking p-waarde met significantie' (Testing of Hypotheses - Further Reading (Dutch) p11).

Z-test voor pi requires n*pi0 > 5 ('slechts benaderd normaal, voorwaarde n*pi0 > 5'; if n*pi0<5 work with the exact distribution of P under H0) (Test Recipes - Further Reading (Dutch) p9-10). chi² 'goodness of fit' test requires e_k > 5 ('slechts benaderd chi², voorwaarde e_k > 5') (Test Recipes p16). chi² 'contingency tables' test requires e_kl > 5, with Yates continuity correction recommended for 2x2 tables (Test Recipes p19-20). The approximate CI for the fraction defectives similarly requires 'n sufficiently large means that at least 5 defectives need to turn up in the sample' (Confidence Intervals.pdf p10).

'voor eenvoud van de testprocedure wordt de keuze van F best gemaakt rekening houdend met de beschikbare kritische waarden in de tabellen (enkel voor probabiliteiten < 0.5)' - i.e. F = s1²/s2² or F = s2²/s1² is chosen so the resulting F-value corresponds to an available (tail probability < 0.5) table entry (Test Recipes - Further Reading (Dutch) p14). Kritische waarden algemeen: F_alpha(n,m) = 1/F_(1-alpha)(m,n) (Test Recipes p12).

conventions.topic: pitfall: setting alpha after seeing the test statistic
conventions.as_stated: 'Set alpha after knowing the test statistic ... destroys the entire meaning of the test... The value of alpha should be said prior to starting the procedure and should be agreed upon between the stakeholders' (Testing of Hypotheses.pdf p11); 'alpha hangt af van economische context en wordt a priori bepaald' (Testing of Hypotheses - Further Reading (Dutch) p6).

conventions.topic: generic 7-step test recipe (universal, applies to any single-sample test)
conventions.as_stated: Step 1: describe the problem as H0 and HA. Step 2: choose significance alpha. Step 3: determine an appropriate test statistic and its sampling distribution. Step 4: find the best sample size, taking into account error risks and practical constraints. Step 5: determine the reference distribution and the critical value (by measuring the significance on the reference distribution). Step 6: draw the sample from the population and determine the value of the test statistic. Step 7: compare the test statistic to the critical value and draw the conclusion. Test recipes differ from each other only in the choice of test statistic and its sampling distribution.

conventions.topic: significance test = (1-confidence) of the equivalent CI
conventions.as_stated: 'When testing with a (1-alpha)x100%-CI, then the significance of the test is alpha' (Confidence Intervals.pdf p13); 'significantie test + betrouwbaarheid interval = 100%' (Testing of Hypotheses - Further Reading (Dutch) p17).

ambiguities.issue: Confidence Intervals.pdf p9, last derivation line reads 'X_bar + t_{0.97 ,n-1} * s/sqrt(n)' where every other line in the same derivation uses 't_{0.975,n-1}'. This looks like a printed typo (missing the digit '5'). Transcribed exactly as printed; treated as 't_0.975,n-1' would be expected/consistent.

Confidence Intervals - Further Reading (Dutch).pdf p15: the pooled-variance formula s_p² is printed with denominator 'n1+n2-1', i.e. 's_p² = [(n1-1)s1²+(n2-1)s2²] / (n1+n2-1)'. This is inconsistent with the standard pooled-variance formula (denominator n1+n2-2) and with the very next line on the same slide, which uses t(n1+n2-2) and the critical value t_{0.025,n1+n2-2} for the resulting 95% CI. Transcribed exactly as printed (verified by re-reading the page image at full resolution); likely a printed typo (n1+n2-1 instead of n1+n2-2).

Confidence Intervals.xlsx sheet 'example t-test', cell F13 (upper CI bound) uses the formula '=F2-F8*F3/SQRT(19)', i.e. dividing by sqrt(19) instead of sqrt(n)=sqrt(20), even though the same workbook's data has n=20 (rows 3-22) and the reference distribution is t(19) (df=19, not n). The corresponding sheet in Testing of Hypotheses.xlsx ('example t-test') computes the test statistic correctly with '=(F2-10)/F3*SQRT(20)'. Both give a value that rounds to the same printed slide value (9.98), so the qualitative conclusion is unaffected, but the exact cached numbers differ: 9.983291415355556 (Confidence Intervals.xlsx, using sqrt(19)) vs. 9.981909129846265 (recomputed with sqrt(20)). Recorded both formula texts as printed; flagging the sqrt(19) denominator as a likely spreadsheet error.

Worked example S03-WE12 (Testing of Hypotheses - Further Reading (Dutch) p22, 'Oefening') is an open exercise for the student; the source provides only the problem setup (H0: pi=0.02 vs HA: pi>0.02, n=400, 10 defectives found) and asks three questions without printing any numeric solution. stated_answers left empty.

Worked example S03-WE17 (Confidence Intervals - Further Reading (Dutch) p23, distribution-free tolerance interval exercise on concrete blocks, n=10, mean=5.8, spreiding=0.15) is presented as an open exercise ('Welke besluit kunnen we dan trekken...?') with no numeric answer printed in the source. stated_answers left empty.
